task.title: Register prepared workflows atomically as inert availability
task.objective: Complete issue https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/680 under decision https://github.com/Knosence9/project-vela/issues/679 by admitting validated topology to a caller-owned process-local registry without making workflows selected or executable.
acceptance_criteria: Provide exact workflow identity, immutable owned topology, exact lookup, and deterministic exact-ID enumeration while retaining authored topology order internally.
Register one homogeneous batch atomically and reject the lexicographically first internal or existing exact-ID collision without mutation.
Reject the first selected non-workflow before filesystem access, reuse complete descriptor-anchored preparation, and mutate the registry only after every conversion succeeds.
Keep registration inert with no selection, transition choice, gate evaluation, action binding, provider call, tool authority, persistence, replacement, or execution.

attempts.summary: Established separate RED coverage for the kernel registry and extension admission bridge.
attempts.diagnostic: The focused kernel test failed because the workflow module and registry contracts did not exist, and the extension test failed because no registration bridge existed.
attempts.patch: Added tests for exact topology preservation and ordering, deterministic lookup, internal and existing collisions, complete atomicity, wrong-kind preflight, sourced preparation failures, and empty filesystem-free registration.

attempts.summary: Implemented one caller-owned registry mutation after complete preparation and conversion.
attempts.diagnostic: Building the full homogeneous batch before collision validation and mutation preserved prior registry state across selection, filesystem, topology, conversion, and collision failures.
attempts.patch: Added immutable kernel workflow topology, WorkflowRegistry::register_all, typed errors, the extension registration bridge, ADR-0007, behavior documentation, and milestone evidence.

attempts.summary: Rejected a rate-limited CodeRabbit false green before merge.
attempts.diagnostic: The initial CodeRabbit result said Review rate limited with a 12-minute cooldown, so its green status could not satisfy the substantive review gate even though local verification and the independent review had passed.
attempts.patch: Kept auto-merge disabled at head d330bd31c5d245fdaf8cf4f749d62138622d366b, waited through cooldown, checked the shared review budget, resumed review once, and merged only after substantive no-actionable-comment coverage and zero unresolved threads.

outcome.summary: Callers can now admit exact validated workflow batches atomically into their own deterministic process-local registry while registration remains availability rather than execution authority.

lessons: Explicit caller-owned registration separates validated availability from discovered metadata and ambient execution behavior.
Atomic admission requires preparing and converting the complete batch before the registry's single mutation point.
Deterministic exact-ID registry order and authored internal topology order serve different contracts and should both be preserved.
A rate-limited green status must not race auto-merge; cooldown, budget check, substantive exact-head review, and zero threads remain mandatory.
Registration grants no provider, tool, action, gate, transition, persistence, replacement, or permission authority.
